claim: Says the character is hiding what he feels, which is a different drawing from simply feeling it. A director uses it whenever the audience must see the effort of concealment — the smile that does not reach the eyes is the whole scene.
method: identical subject sentence and seed in every panel; only the option clause changes. panels marked control render the untouched subject, because SDXL cannot express absence.

panels.clause: suppressed expression, tight lips, tense jaw
forced smile, strained smile, unsmiling eyes
trembling lips, wavering expression, crumpling face
exaggerated smile, theatrical expression, showy pose

review.issue: fake_calm ("expressionless, flat smile, tense shoulders") and deadpan ("deadpan, expressionless, half-closed eyes") share the dominant tag "expressionless" and will land close together. fake_calm is also internally contradictory — "expressionless" and "flat smile" ask for two different mouths, and the model will pick one.
review.fix: Give fake_calm a mask that reads as effort rather than absence: "calm expression, closed mouth, tense shoulders, sweatdrop" (sweatdrop is a strong danbooru tag and is exactly anime's notation for composure under strain). Keep "expressionless" exclusive to deadpan.

look_at: The effort of concealment reads: forced_smile, breaking, deadpan, performative all land.
